domain: California contractor licensing, home improvement contracts, enforcement and contractor business compliance (CSLB)
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), PDF pages 1-46: front matter, Summary of Recent Changes (2025 legislation effective 2026), Sections Affected by 2025 Legislation, CSLB background, Ch. 1 Enforcement (complaints and citations), Ch. 2 Home Improvement, Ch. 3 Managing a Business (business forms, taxes/permits, bonds, insurance, workers' compensation)

rules.title: Home improvement down payment cap: lesser of $1,000 or 10%
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, the down payment cannot be more than $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors (and their salespersons) on residential home improvement contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: The down payment ... may not exceed $1,000 or 10 percent of the contract price, whichever is less.
rules.notes: Chapter 2 is a summary; full statutory text (Chapter 8, not in this chunk) may contain special cases (e.g., swimming pool contracts) - verify against B&P 7159/7159.5 full text. CSLB lists excessive down payments as a common complaint and contract problem (PDF pages 24, 36).

rules.title: No payment ahead of completed work or delivered materials
rules.plain_english: Apart from the down payment, you cannot demand or accept payment for work or materials until that work is done or those materials are delivered.

payment_allowed_when: work for that payment is completed
materials for that payment are delivered

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors on home improvement contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: Except for a down payment, a contractor cannot demand or accept payment for work or materials until the work is completed or the materials are delivered.
rules.notes: A payment-schedule checker can flag any progress payment due before the corresponding work/material milestone.

rules.title: Contract and all changes must be written and signed by all parties
rules.plain_english: The home improvement contract and every change to it (change orders) must be in writing, legible, and signed by everyone involved.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and change orders
rules.verbatim_quote: The contract and any changes to the contract must be in writing and signed by all parties. The writing must be legible and printed forms must be readable.
rules.notes: CSLB lists 'Change orders not included' as a common contract problem (PDF page 36).

rules.title: Contracts and changes must be legible, understandable and state the cancellation right
rules.plain_english: Any change to a home improvement contract must be written, legible and easy to understand, and the consumer must be told of their right to cancel or rescind.

parameters.must_inform_of: consumer's right to cancel or rescind

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and changes to them
rules.verbatim_quote: The following rules are required for improvement contracts: any changes made to contracts must be in writing, be legible, be easy to understand, and inform a consumer of their right to cancel or rescind the contract; and a home improvement contract must contain various information, notices, and disclosures for the protection of the consumer.
rules.notes: Summary text; sentence structure is ambiguous whether the 'inform of right to cancel' requirement attaches to changes or to the contract generally. Treat as applying to the contract (and conservatively to change documents).

rules.title: Give buyer a signed, dated copy before work starts
rules.plain_english: Before starting any work, give the homeowner a copy of the contract signed and dated by both you and the homeowner.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors on home improvement contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: Before any work is started, the contractor must give the buyer a copy of the contract signed and dated by both the contractor and the buyer.
rules.notes: Workflow gate: block 'start work' status until signed copy delivery is recorded.

rules.title: Minimum 10-point type; 10-point bold headings
rules.plain_english: Printed home improvement contract text must be at least 10-point type and headings at least 10-point bold, unless the law requires something larger for a specific notice.

parameters.override: larger size where a specific notice requires it

rules.applies_to: Printed home improvement contract forms, notices and disclosures
rules.verbatim_quote: Unless a larger typeface is specified in the law referenced above, text in any printed form shall be in at least 10-point typeface and the headings shall be in at least 10-point boldface type.
rules.notes: Also stated on PDF page 31. Specific notices with larger type requirements are in the full B&P 7159 text (Chapter 8), not in this chunk.

rules.title: Salesperson commission paid pro rata with payments
rules.plain_english: If a salesperson's commission is built into the contract price, pay the salesperson in proportion to the payments the contractor actually receives.

parameters.trigger: salesperson commission included in contract price
parameters.payout_method: pro rata to contractor payment schedule

rules.verbatim_quote: If the contract includes a salesperson’s commission in the contract price, the payment to the salesperson shall be made on a pro rata basis in proportion to the schedule of payments made to the contractor.
rules.notes: Formula is a direct arithmetic reading of 'pro rata ... in proportion to the schedule of payments'.

rules.title: Contract must show salesperson name and HIS registration number
rules.plain_english: The home improvement contract must list the salesperson's name and their CSLB salesperson registration number.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts sold through a salesperson
rules.verbatim_quote: The contract must contain the name and registration number of the salesperson.
rules.notes: Missing HIS registration numbers is listed as a common contract problem (PDF page 36).

rules.title: Contract must show contractor name, business address and license number
rules.plain_english: Put your business name, business address and CSLB license number on the home improvement contract.
rules.verbatim_quote: The name, business address, and license number of the contractor must be included.
rules.notes: Effective 2026-01-01, contractor email address is also required (AB 1327) - see hic-contractor-email-required.

rules.title: Required descriptive sections of a home improvement contract
rules.plain_english: The contract must fully describe the work, materials and equipment, price, payment schedule, start and completion dates, permits and tests, permissible delays, extra work, mechanics' lien release statements, and the owner's right to cancel.

required_sections: Start and completion of work (dates and descriptions)
Required release of mechanics’ liens statements

rules.verbatim_quote: Contract must include full descriptions and information about the following: • Description of work • Description of materials and equipment • The contract price • Payment schedule • Start and completion of work (dates and descriptions) • Permits and tests • Permissible delays • Extra work • Required release of mechanics’ liens statements • Owner’s applicable right to cancellation
rules.notes: Book says this list is not complete; see full B&P 7159 in Chapter 8 for exact wording and subdivision numbers.

rules.title: Required notices and disclosures in home improvement and pool contracts
rules.plain_english: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts must include the full text of several notices: extra work/change orders, CGL insurance, workers' comp insurance, extra/change-order work notice, mechanics lien warning, Contractors Board information, and right to cancel with Notice of Cancellation instructions.

required_notices: Performance of Extra or Change-Order Work Notice
Applicable Right to Cancel and Notice of Cancellation Instructions
parameters.placement: some in main body, others may be attached separately

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and swimming pool contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts in California are required to have the full text of several notices and disclosures. Some must be in the main body of the contract; others may be attached separately.
rules.notes: Full notice text and which notices must be in the body vs attached are NOT in this chunk (see Chapter 8 B&P 7159). 'Missing notices and/or disclosures' is CSLB's first-listed common contract problem.

rules.title: Contract must include contractor's email address (AB 1327)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, home improvement contracts must include the contractor's email address.
rules.citation: B&P 7159 (as amended by AB 1327, Ch. 348, Stats. 2025)
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill requires home improvement contracts (HIC) to include the contractor’s email address and allow for cancelation of the HIC by the buyer via email.
rules.notes: Bill summary; exact statutory wording/placement in B&P 7159 full text (Chapter 8).

rules.title: Buyer may cancel home improvement contract by email (AB 1327)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, the homeowner must be allowed to cancel the home improvement contract by email.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and their Notice of Cancellation
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill requires home improvement contracts (HIC) to include the contractor’s email address and allow for cancelation of the HIC by the buyer via email.
rules.notes: Cancellation period lengths (e.g., 3-day/5-day) are not stated in this chunk; see Civil Code 1689.6/1689.7 and B&P 7159 full text. AB 1327 also amends B&P 17511.5.

rules.title: Contract must include phone number for help with Notice of Cancellation (AB 1327)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, the contract must give a telephone number the homeowner can call for help finding and filling out the Notice of Cancellation.

required_fields: telephone number to assist buyer with Notice of Cancellation

rules.citation: B&P 7159; Civ. Code 1689.6, 1689.7 (as amended by AB 1327)
rules.verbatim_quote: The bill requires the HIC to include a telephone number to assist the buyer in locating and filling out the “Notice of Cancellation.”
rules.notes: Whose number (contractor's or CSLB's) is not specified in this summary; check full text.

rules.title: Missing Notice of Cancellation is grounds for CSLB complaint (AB 1327)
rules.plain_english: The Notice of Cancellation must be included in or attached to the contract; if it is missing, the homeowner can file a complaint with CSLB.

parameters.placement: included in or attached to the HIC
parameters.consequence_if_missing: buyer may file complaint with CSLB

rules.citation: B&P 7159; Civ. Code 1689.6, 1689.7 (as amended by AB 1327)
rules.verbatim_quote: The bill also provides that if the “Notice of Cancellation” is not included in or attached to the HIC, the buyer may file a complaint with the Contractors State License Board (CSLB).

rules.title: Disclose subcontractors on consumer request (SB 517)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, if the homeowner asks, you must disclose any subcontractors on the job and give each one's name, contact information, license number and classification.
rules.applies_to: Prime/direct contractors on home improvement contracts using subcontractors
rules.citation: B&P 7159 (as amended by SB 517, Ch. 585, Stats. 2025)
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill requires the disclosure of the use of any subcontractors in a home improvement contract upon request by the consumer and for the subcontractor’s name, contact information, license number, and classification to be provided.
rules.notes: Also described on PDF page 31. Response deadline after request is not stated in this chunk.

rules.title: Prime/direct contractor responsible for the project (SB 517)
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement job the prime (direct) contractor is responsible for the whole project, but subcontractors and salespersons can still be disciplined for their own violations.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement projects with subcontractors or salespersons
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 15 (also PDF page 31)
rules.verbatim_quote: the prime or direct contractor is responsible for the construction project; however, it does not preclude administrative discipline against any subcontractor or home improvement salesperson for violations of Contractors State License Law.

rules.title: Service and repair contract for jobs of $750 or less
rules.plain_english: For jobs of $750 or less, a licensed contractor uses a 'service and repair contract' instead of a full home improvement contract, but only if the contract meets all four statutory requirements.

parameters.fallback_if_conditions_not_met: full home improvement contract requirements apply regardless of price

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors doing small residential service/repair jobs
rules.citation: B&P 7150-7159.9 et seq. (service and repair contract provisions; specific section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition, a “service and repair contract” must be used by licensed contractors for jobs of $750 or less, provided that the contract meets all four of the new requirements.
rules.notes: The four requirements and the service-and-repair disclosures are NOT listed in this chunk (see Chapter 8, Home Improvement Business). Commonly codified at B&P 7159.10 et seq. - verify.

rules.title: Non-compliant service and repair contract is treated as a home improvement contract
rules.plain_english: If a service and repair contract does not meet its specific requirements, all home improvement contract rules apply to it no matter how small the price.

parameters.condition: service and repair contract fails specified requirements

rules.citation: B&P 7150-7159.9 et seq. (service and repair contract provisions)
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition, a service and repair contract that does not meet specified requirements is subject to the requirements applicable to a home improvement contract regardless of the aggregate contract price.

rules.title: Violating home improvement or service and repair contract law is grounds for discipline
rules.plain_english: Any violation of the home improvement or service and repair contract rules can lead to CSLB discipline against the contractor.

parameters.trigger: any violation of HIC or service and repair contract provisions

rules.verbatim_quote: Any violation of the provisions of law applicable to home improvement and service and repair contracts subject the contractor to discipline.

rules.title: CSLB list of common home improvement contract problems (compliance checklist)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's list of frequent contract defects is a ready-made checklist: missing notices, excessive down payment, vague materials/equipment, unclear start/completion dates, unclear price, missing change orders, missing license/HIS numbers, permits not identified or not saying who pays, and no payment schedule.

checks: equipment detailed and materials specifically described
start and completion information clearly stated including dates
required building permits identified and who pays for them stated

rules.verbatim_quote: Common Problems with Home Improvement Contracts • Missing notices and/or disclosures • Excessive down payment requested or received • Equipment to be used or installed is not detailed, and materials to be used not described specifically • Job start and completion information not clearly stated and described including dates
rules.notes: Remaining items on the page: bid or price not carefully or completely established; change orders not included; license number and HIS registration numbers missing; failure to identify required building permits or indicate who is paying for them; no payment schedule.

rules.title: Definition of home improvement
rules.plain_english: Home improvement means repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, modernizing or adding to residential property, including driveways, pools/spas, patios, solar, landscaping, fences, garages and similar work next to a dwelling, plus installing home improvement goods or services.

included_examples: swimming pools (including spas and hot tubs)
other improvements of structures or land adjacent to a dwelling

rules.applies_to: Classifying whether a residential job is home improvement (triggers HIC rules)
rules.citation: B&P 7150-7159.9 (Home Improvement; definition section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: Home improvement is the repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, or modernizing of, or adding to, residential property ... Home improvement is also the installation of home improvement goods or the furnishing of home improvement services.
rules.notes: Statutory definition is commonly B&P 7151 - not cited on this page.

rules.title: Definition of home improvement contractor
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor (including a swimming pool contractor) is any CSLB-licensed contractor doing home improvement work, full-time or part-time.
rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement contractor, including a swimming pool contractor, is a contractor licensed by the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) who is engaged in the business of home improvement either full-time or part-time.

rules.title: Home roof warranties transfer to later buyers unless conspicuously limited
rules.plain_english: For roofing contracts signed on or after Jan 1, 1994, the roof warranty automatically benefits later owners of the home unless the contract has a clear and conspicuous clause limiting transfer.

parameters.beneficiaries: all subsequent purchasers and transferees of the residential structure
parameters.to_limit_transfer: clear and conspicuous provision in contract

rules.applies_to: Roofing contractors issuing home roof warranties on residential structures
rules.verbatim_quote: For any contract subject to this chapter that is entered into on or after January 1, 1994, the warranty obligations shall inure to the benefit of, and shall be directly enforceable by, all subsequent purchasers and transferees of the residential structure, without limitation, unless the contract contains a clear and conspicuous provision limiting transferability of the warranty
rules.notes: Book states home warranties generally are not transferable except home roof warranties as provided here.

rules.title: Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration required
rules.plain_english: Anyone who sells, solicits, negotiates or signs home improvement contracts for a contractor away from the contractor's normal place of business must be registered with CSLB as a Home Improvement Salesperson, no matter the contract amount.

parameters.location_trigger: outside the contractor's normal place of business

rules.applies_to: Salespeople of licensed home improvement contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Anyone who solicits, sells, negotiates, or executes home improvement contracts for a licensed contractor outside of the contractor’s normal place of business, regardless of the dollar amount of these contracts, must be registered with CSLB as a Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS).
rules.notes: B&P 7152 ('Home improvement salesperson' definition) was amended by 2025 legislation (Ch. 592) per Sections Affected table (PDF page 16); amended text not in this chunk.

rules.title: Notify CSLB before employing a registered HIS and when employment ends
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor must notify CSLB in writing before employing an already-registered salesperson, and again in writing when that salesperson's employment ends.

notice_1.when: prior to employing an already registered HIS

notice_2.when: when employment of a registered HIS ends

parameters.forms: CSLB HIS forms (www.cslb.ca.gov, search: HIS forms)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors employing home improvement salespersons
rules.citation: B&P 7150-7170 (HIS provisions; specific section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: Licensees are required to notify CSLB in writing prior to employing an already registered HIS and to notify CSLB in writing when employment of a registered HIS ends.
rules.notes: No day-count deadline for the end-of-employment notice is stated in this chunk.

rules.title: Who is exempt from HIS registration
rules.plain_english: You don't need HIS registration if you only sell at a fixed showroom, are listed official personnel on the license, only schedule appointments for a registered HIS, or are a service/repair employee limited to the repair the customer requested.

exempt: salespersons selling goods or negotiating only at a fixed business establishment where goods/services are exhibited or offered
official personnel of record on the license (individual contractor, qualifiers, partners, corporate officers, RMOs, LLC members/managers/employees listed)
persons who only contact buyers to schedule appointments for a registered HIS
bona fide service or repair employees of a licensed contractor whose calls are limited to the service/repair initially requested

rules.verbatim_quote: Salespersons who only sell goods or negotiate contracts at a fixed business establishment where the goods or services are exhibited or offered for sale are not considered home improvement salespeople.

rules.title: HIS qualifications: age 18+, fingerprints
rules.plain_english: A home improvement salesperson must be at least 18 and submit fingerprints; there are no education, residency or experience requirements.
rules.verbatim_quote: A home improvement salesperson must be at least 18 years old. There are no educational, residency, or experience requirements. However, a home improvement salesperson must submit their fingerprints to CSLB as part of the application process.

rules.title: HIS application fee $200 (nonrefundable)
rules.plain_english: The HIS registration application fee is $200, nonrefundable and nontransferable.
rules.citation: B&P 7137 (fee schedule) - not cited on this page
rules.verbatim_quote: Submit the required nonrefundable, nontransferable application fee of $200 and your application to the CSLB headquarters office.
rules.notes: B&P 7137 fee schedule was amended by 2025 legislation (Ch. 592) per PDF page 16; confirm the current fee against the fee schedule in Chapter 8.

rules.title: No HIS work until CSLB issues registration number
rules.plain_english: A salesperson cannot start selling home improvement contracts just by applying; they must wait until CSLB issues a registration number.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement salesperson applicants and contractors who would employ them
rules.verbatim_quote: No. CSLB must review your application and issue a registration number before you may legally work as a home improvement salesperson.
rules.notes: Citation inferred from the misdemeanor rule on PDF page 34 (acting as HIS without registration).

rules.title: HIS registration expires 2 years from end of issue month
rules.plain_english: A salesperson registration expires two years after the last day of the month it was issued.

parameters.anchor: last day of the month of issuance

rules.verbatim_quote: The HIS registration expires two years from the last day of the month in which it was issued.
rules.notes: CSLB mails a renewal application several weeks before expiration.

rules.title: HIS must report address change within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A registered salesperson must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days of changing address.
rules.verbatim_quote: If your address has changed since your registration was issued or last renewed, it is your responsibility to notify CSLB in writing within 90 days of the change.

rules.title: Contact CSLB if no renewal notice 3 weeks before HIS expiry
rules.plain_english: If a salesperson hasn't received the renewal notice, they should contact CSLB no later than three weeks before the registration expires.
rules.verbatim_quote: If you have not received an advance notification of renewal, notify CSLB. This should be done no later than three weeks before your registration expires.
rules.notes: Phrased as 'should' - CSLB guidance rather than a statutory penalty deadline.

rules.title: Contractor discipline for employing unregistered salesperson
rules.plain_english: A contractor who uses an unregistered person to negotiate home improvement contracts can be disciplined by CSLB.

parameters.violation: employing unregistered person to negotiate home improvement contracts

rules.verbatim_quote: According to B&P Code section 7154, a contractor who employs an unregistered person to negotiate home improvement contracts is subject to disciplinary action by the registrar.
rules.notes: PDF page 29: unregistered salespersons are cited using the same citation process as unlicensed contractors, and the employing contractor may also be disciplined.

rules.title: Acting as a salesperson without registration is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: Working as a home improvement salesperson without CSLB registration is a misdemeanor and can also bring an administrative citation.
rules.verbatim_quote: Furthermore, B&P Code section 7153 states that it is a misdemeanor for a person to act as a home improvement salesperson without being registered.
rules.notes: Citation process for unregistered HIS follows the unlicensed-contractor process (PDF page 29), including the 15-working-day appeal window.

rules.title: Contractor may not have an interest in the joint control company
rules.plain_english: If you provide a joint control (funds control) arrangement as part of a home improvement contract, you cannot have any financial or other interest in the joint control company.

parameters.prohibited: any financial or other interest in the joint control company

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using joint control agreements
rules.citation: B&P Code joint control provisions (section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors who furnish a joint control as part of the terms of a home improvement contract should be aware that the law prohibits them from having any financial or other interest in the joint control company.
rules.notes: CSLB does not license, list, or monitor joint control companies. Joint control must be registrar-approved 'covering full performance and payment'. CSLB advises consulting an attorney first.

rules.title: Citation civil penalty up to $8,000 (most) / $30,000 (serious)
rules.plain_english: A CSLB citation can order you to correct the work, pay restitution, and pay a civil penalty of up to $8,000 for most violations, or up to $30,000 for serious violations of B&P 7110, 7114, 7118 and 7125.4.
rules.verbatim_quote: If a more serious violation is established, the registrar of contractors may issue a citation, which can include an order to correct a project, make restitution to an injured party, and pay a civil penalty of up to $8,000 for most violations, and up to $30,000 for serious violations.
rules.notes: Per PDF page 16, B&P 7099.2 is repealed and replaced effective July 1, 2026 (new version adds minimum penalties and CPI adjustments); confirm maxima against operative text. CCR 883 (order of correction - extension of time to correct) was amended in 2025.

rules.title: Process to contest a citation (licensed contractor)
rules.plain_english: If you contest a citation, CSLB may hold an informal citation conference; if unresolved, an administrative law judge hearing follows. If you lose and don't comply with the final citation, your license can be suspended and then revoked.

steps: comply (no further action) OR contest all/part
if licensee loses and does not comply with final order: suspension, then revocation

rules.verbatim_quote: If the licensee contests all or any part of the citation, an informal citation conference may be held to resolve the citation. If the matter is not settled, a hearing can be set before an administrative law judge of the State of California.
rules.notes: The deadline to contest a citation issued to a licensee is not stated in this chunk (the 15-working-day rule on PDF page 28 is stated for unlicensed persons).

rules.title: Advisory notice and letter of admonishment (disclosed 1-2 years)
rules.plain_english: For minor violations CSLB may send an advisory notice; for some violations it may issue a letter of admonishment, which can require a corrective action plan and is publicly shown on the license for one or two years.

parameters.advisory_notice: isolated or minor violations; warns of stricter action on repeat

rules.citation: B&P 7099.2 (letter of admonishment per section title, PDF page 16)
rules.verbatim_quote: For some violations, CSLB may issue a letter of admonishment. This may require the licensee to submit a corrective action plan showing compliance with the law and is publicly disclosable on the license record for one or two years.

rules.title: Accusation for flagrant violations
rules.plain_english: For flagrant violations, CSLB files an accusation through the Attorney General to suspend or revoke the license; the case may settle (stipulation) or go to an administrative law judge, and blatant violations can be referred to the district attorney.

steps: stipulated settlement OR hearing before administrative law judge

rules.citation: B&P disciplinary proceedings (sections not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: For flagrant violations of law, the registrar will take administrative action by filing an accusation with the state attorney general stating the board’s intent to suspend or revoke the license.
rules.notes: Outcomes listed on PDF pages 26-27.

rules.title: Revoked license: 1-5 year bar plus disciplinary bond
rules.plain_english: A revoked license cannot be reinstated or reissued for one to five years from the decision; involved personnel are also barred, and reinstatement requires complying with the decision, settling losses and filing a disciplinary bond.

parameters.personnel_barred: official personnel who knew of or participated in the violation
reinstatement_conditions: comply with all provisions of decision
file disciplinary bond in amount set by registrar

rules.applies_to: Licensees and their personnel of record
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensee’s right to contract is taken away. The license shall not be reinstated or reissued for one to five years from the effective date of the decision.
rules.notes: Disciplinary bond amount is set by the registrar - no fixed number in this chunk.

rules.title: Suspension and probation require a disciplinary bond
rules.plain_english: A suspended licensee cannot operate and must file a disciplinary bond before reinstatement; a licensee on probation must follow its terms and file a disciplinary bond to stay in business.
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensee is not entitled to operate during the period of suspension. A disciplinary bond must be filed before the license is reinstated or reissued.
rules.notes: Probation text: 'They also must file a disciplinary bond to remain in business during this period.'

rules.title: Pay investigation and enforcement costs to keep or renew license
rules.plain_english: If ordered, you must pay CSLB's investigation and enforcement costs to stay in good standing or to renew or reinstate your license.
rules.citation: B&P disciplinary provisions (section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensee, to maintain good and clear standing or as a condition for renewal and reinstatement of their license, must pay the costs as ordered or as stipulated.

rules.title: When complaints are publicly disclosed
rules.plain_english: Once CSLB finds a probable violation serious enough for suspension or revocation, the complaint's date, nature and status are shown publicly with a disclaimer; dismissed matters are not disclosed.

parameters.disclosure_trigger: probable violation presenting risk of harm for which suspension/revocation would be appropriate

rules.verbatim_quote: Once CSLB has determined that a probable violation of law has occurred, which, if proven, would present a risk of harm to the public—and for which suspension or revocation of the contractor’s license would be appropriate—the date, nature, and status of the complaint will be disclosed to the public.
rules.notes: Citation section number is not stated on the page; B&P 7124.6 is the usual disclosure section - verify.

rules.title: Citations disclosed for 5 years after compliance
rules.plain_english: A citation appears on the public license record from issuance until five years after you comply with it.
rules.verbatim_quote: Citations will be disclosed to the public from date of issuance and for five years from the date of compliance.
rules.notes: Citation section number not stated on the page.

rules.title: Accusations disclosed 7 years after settlement; revocations indefinitely
rules.plain_english: Accusations that end in suspension or stayed revocation are public from filing until seven years after settlement; non-stayed revocations are public indefinitely.
rules.verbatim_quote: Accusations that result in suspension or stayed revocation of the contractor license shall be disclosed from the date the accusation is filed and for seven years after the accusation has been settled, including the terms and conditions of probation. All revocations that are not stayed shall be disclosed indefinitely from the effective date of the revocation.

rules.title: Contracting without a license is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a crime (misdemeanor) to do or offer contracting work without a CSLB license unless you fit an exemption in B&P 7040-7054.5.

parameters.violation: engaging in business or acting as contractor without license

rules.applies_to: Anyone performing or offering construction contracting in California; owners hiring them
rules.verbatim_quote: In California, it is a misdemeanor to engage in the business or act in the capacity of a contractor without a contractor license unless the contractor meets the criteria for exemption specified in Business and Professions Code sections 7040 through 7054.5.
rules.notes: The misdemeanor section itself (commonly B&P 7028) is not cited on this page. New 2026 exemption: murals (B&P 7050). B&P 7048 minor-work exemption amended in 2025.

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor citation: cease-and-desist plus penalty up to $15,000
rules.plain_english: CSLB can cite an unlicensed (or suspended/not-current) contractor with an order to stop and a civil penalty of up to $15,000.

parameters.applies_when: no license in good standing (current and not suspended)

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons and contractors without a license in good standing; also unregistered HIS
rules.verbatim_quote: The citation includes an order of abatement to cease and desist and a civil penalty of up to $15,000.
rules.notes: The $1,500 minimum is from SB 779 (PDF page 15), commencing July 1, 2026. Section number taken from Sections Affected table (PDF page 16, 7028.7 'Unlicensed contracting; Citation and penalties').

rules.title: Appeal unlicensed citation within 15 working days
rules.plain_english: A cited unlicensed person must get a written appeal to CSLB within 15 working days after the citation is served, or it becomes a final order.

parameters.requirement: written appeal received by the board
parameters.consequence_if_missed: citation becomes final order of the registrar

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed contractors and unregistered home improvement salespersons who are cited
rules.verbatim_quote: Unless the board receives a written appeal within 15 working days after the citation is served, the citation becomes a final order of the registrar.
rules.notes: Deadline is based on board receipt, not mailing. Appeal path: informal settlement conference, then administrative law judge.

rules.title: CSLB options against unlicensed contractors
rules.plain_english: Against unlicensed contractors CSLB can issue a citation, refer for criminal prosecution (fine, probation, restitution, jail), or seek a court injunction; continuing to contract after a citation can lead to a DA referral.

options: injunction via Attorney General or district attorney
injunction_venue: county where unlicensed person has business or residence

rules.citation: B&P 7028.7 and related (not all cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: When the board receives a complaint against an unlicensed contractor, it may issue an administrative citation or file a criminal action with the local district attorney’s office. In some cases, it may initiate injunction proceedings against the unlicensed person through the Office of the Attorney General or the district attorney.

rules.title: Be ready to show proof of license on any jobsite (SWIFT)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's SWIFT team can visit any jobsite without a complaint, demand proof of a license in good standing, and cite anyone not properly licensed.

parameters.document: proof of licensure in good standing

rules.verbatim_quote: SWIFT has the authority to visit any jobsite without cause or complaint, ask contractors to produce proof of licensure in good standing, and cite those who are not properly licensed.

rules.title: CSLB complaint handling steps
rules.plain_english: When a complaint is filed, CSLB notifies the contractor to try to resolve it, may request documents and attempt mediation, and may then recommend arbitration, a bond claim, small claims or a civil suit, or open an investigation.

steps: confirmation to complainant and notice to contractor
recommend CSLB arbitration / contact bond surety / small claims / superior court

rules.verbatim_quote: If appropriate, CSLB will attempt mediation. If mediation is unsuccessful, CSLB may recommend settlement through its arbitration program, recommend that the complainant contact the surety company that issued the contractor’s bond, file a claim in small claims court, or file a civil suit in superior court.

rules.title: Common grounds for complaints against contractors
rules.plain_english: Typical complaint triggers include poor workmanship, abandonment, not paying subs/suppliers/employees, code violations, lack of diligence, deceptive advertising, excessive down payments or missing payment schedules, no workers' comp, and home improvement contract violations.

risk_items: failure to pay subcontractors, suppliers, or employees
failure to obtain workers’ compensation insurance
violations of home improvement contract law

rules.verbatim_quote: Common complaints made against contractors involve poor workmanship; abandonment of a project; failure to pay subcontractors, suppliers, or employees; building code violations; lack of reasonable diligence in executing a construction project; use of false, misleading, or deceptive advertising;
rules.notes: Remaining items in the sentence: excessive down payments or not including payment schedules in HICs; failure to obtain workers’ compensation insurance; violations of home improvement contract law.

rules.title: Verify contractor license, bond and workers' comp online
rules.plain_english: Owners and prime contractors can look up any contractor (or HIS) on CSLB's website by license number, name or business name to check status, legal actions, classifications, bond and workers' comp.
rules.applies_to: Project owners, general contractors vetting subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: CSLB’s website, www.cslb.ca.gov or www.CheckTheLicenseFirst.com, provides the ability to look ... up a contractor by license number, name, or business name, and obtain the licensee’s contact information, license status, CSLB legal actions (if any), classifications held, business type, and bond and workers’ compensation insurance information.
rules.notes: Useful as an automated pre-hire / pre-subcontract verification step.

rules.title: CSLB has 45 license classifications
rules.plain_english: CSLB licenses contractors in 45 classifications covering the construction industry.
rules.verbatim_quote: CSLB licenses and regulates contractors in 45 license classifications that constitute the construction industry.
rules.notes: Classification list itself is not in this chunk (Chapter 9). 16 CCR 832 reference is outside this chunk - verify.

rules.title: Attorney General may seek license discipline for unpaid wages (AB 1002)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, the Attorney General can sue to suspend, revoke or deny a contractor's license for failing to pay workers or ignoring a wage judgment or court order.

triggers: failure to comply with wage judgment or court order

rules.verbatim_quote: This bill authorizes the Attorney General (AG) to file a civil action to suspend, revoke, or deny licensure of a contractor for failure to pay workers or failure to comply with a wage judgment or court order.
rules.notes: CSLB may intervene or collaborate in the AG proceeding.

rules.title: CSLB not liable for attorney fees on cash-deposit bond claims (AB 521)
rules.plain_english: A contractor may file a cash deposit with CSLB instead of a license bond; starting 2026, CSLB is not liable for attorney fees in civil claims against that deposit.

parameters.bond_alternative: cash deposit filed with CSLB in lieu of license bond

rules.applies_to: Contractors using a cash deposit instead of a surety license bond; claimants against it
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill expressly provides that CSLB is not liable for attorney fees in civil claims involving a contractor’s cash deposit filed with CSLB in lieu of a license bond.
rules.notes: Liability allocation rule; no dollar amounts stated.

rules.title: Higher civil penalties for workers' comp violations (SB 291)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, civil penalties for workers' compensation violations are significantly increased.
rules.verbatim_quote: The bill significantly increases civil penalties for violations of workers’ compensation (WC) requirements and prohibits CSLB from renewing or reinstating a license in violation of WC requirements until the applicant or licensee provides a current and valid WC certificate.
rules.notes: Specific penalty amounts are NOT stated in this chunk; see B&P 7099.2 (operative July 1, 2026) at book page 317. Do not compute without the operative text.

rules.title: No license renewal/reinstatement without valid WC certificate (SB 291)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, CSLB will not renew or reinstate a license that is out of compliance with workers' comp rules until a current, valid workers' comp certificate is provided.

parameters.document: current and valid workers’ compensation certificate

rules.citation: B&P 7125.4 / 7125.7 (as amended by SB 291; exact section not stated)
rules.verbatim_quote: The bill significantly increases civil penalties for violations of workers’ compensation (WC) requirements and prohibits CSLB from renewing or reinstating a license in violation of WC requirements until the applicant or licensee provides a current and valid WC certificate.
rules.notes: Renewal workflow should check WC certificate (or valid exemption) status before submission.

rules.title: CSLB to verify workers' comp exemption eligibility (SB 291)
rules.plain_english: CSLB must create an evidence-based process to verify that contractors claiming a workers' comp exemption actually qualify, and report to the Legislature by January 1, 2027.
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill also requires CSLB to determine an evidence-based process and procedure to verify eligibility for a workers’ compensation (WC) insurance exemption and to report its findings to the Legislature by January 1, 2027.
rules.notes: The 2027-01-01 date is CSLB's reporting deadline, not a contractor filing deadline. Contractors claiming exemptions should expect evidence requests; process details not in this chunk.

rules.title: Mural artists exempt from contractor licensing (SB 456)
rules.plain_english: Starting 2026, artists who paint, apply, restore or conserve a mural under an agreement with someone authorized to approve the work do not need a contractor license.

parameters.subject: mural
parameters.condition: agreement with a person who can legally authorize the work

rules.verbatim_quote: This bill exempts artists who draw, paint, apply, execute, restore or conserve a mural pursuant to an agreement with a person who can legally authorize the work from licensure.
rules.notes: See mural-definition.

rules.title: Definition of mural for licensing exemption
rules.plain_english: A 'mural' is a unique, hand-drawn or hand-painted work of fine art protected by copyright, trademark, label or patent, applied directly to a building's wall, ceiling, fixture or appurtenance; painted wall signs are not murals.

must_be: protected by copyright, trademark, label, or patent
directly upon interior/exterior wall, ceiling, fixture, or other appurtenance of building/structure

rules.applies_to: Determining whether the mural exemption applies
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill also defines a “mural” as a unique work of fine art that is protected by copyright, trademark, label, or patent and that is drawn or painted by hand directly upon an interior or exterior wall or ceiling, fixture, or other appurtenances of a building or structure. Additionally, this bill provides that a mural does not include painted wall signs.

rules.title: Minimum $1,500 civil penalty for unlicensed activity from July 1, 2026 (SB 779)
rules.plain_english: Starting July 1, 2026, citations for violations involving unlicensed persons carry a minimum civil penalty of $1,500.
rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons (and possibly those aiding them) cited by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill, commencing July 1, 2026, would increase the minimum civil penalties for violations related to unlicensed persons to at least $1,500 and would impose minimum civil penalties of at least $500 or $1,500 for other specified violations, as provided.
rules.notes: Maximum remains as stated elsewhere ($15,000 per PDF page 28) unless changed by the operative text - verify.

rules.title: Minimum citation penalties of $500 or $1,500 for other violations (SB 779)
rules.plain_english: Starting July 1, 2026, other specified citation violations carry minimum civil penalties of either $500 or $1,500.
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill, commencing July 1, 2026, would increase the minimum civil penalties for violations related to unlicensed persons to at least $1,500 and would impose minimum civil penalties of at least $500 or $1,500 for other specified violations, as provided.
rules.notes: Which violations get $500 vs $1,500 is NOT specified in this chunk; see B&P 7099.2 full text (book page 317).

rules.title: Minimum fines may be raised by CPI every five years (SB 779)
rules.plain_english: CSLB may raise minimum citation fine amounts based on Consumer Price Index increases every five years.
rules.citation: B&P 7099.2 (operative July 1, 2026; 'Civil penalty assessment; Factors and inflation adjustments')
rules.verbatim_quote: This bill establishes and increases minimum fine amounts included with enforcement citations and allows CSLB to raise minimum fine amounts based on increases to the Consumer Price Index every five years.
rules.notes: Penalty tables should be versioned by effective date to absorb CPI adjustments.

rules.title: Minor work (small contract) exemption B&P 7048 amended in 2025
rules.plain_english: The exemption for small contracts under a set dollar amount (B&P 7048) was amended by 2025 legislation; check the current threshold before relying on it.
rules.applies_to: Unlicensed handypersons and owners hiring them for small jobs
rules.verbatim_quote: Contracts aggregating less than 7048 specified amount; When exemption Amended 67 245 not applicable
rules.notes: Only the section title appears in this chunk (Sections Affected table); the dollar threshold and conditions are NOT stated here. Do not hard-code a number from this source.

rules.title: Holder of inactive license may not contract (B&P 7076.5 amended)
rules.plain_english: A contractor holding an inactive license certificate is not entitled to practice contracting until reinstated; this section was amended in 2025.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with inactive licenses; owners verifying license status
rules.verbatim_quote: Inactive license certificate; 7076.5 Reinstatement; Holder not entitled Amended 592 297 to practice
rules.notes: Derived from section title in the Sections Affected table; substantive changes not described in this chunk.

rules.title: CSLB fee schedule (B&P 7137) amended in 2025
rules.plain_english: CSLB's fee schedule was amended by 2025 legislation; license, renewal and registration fees should be checked against the current schedule.
rules.verbatim_quote: 7137 Fee schedule Amended 592 351
rules.notes: Fee amounts are NOT in this chunk. The $200 HIS fee on PDF page 33 should be cross-checked.

rules.title: Definition of incidental and supplemental work (16 CCR 831) amended
rules.plain_english: The regulation defining 'incidental and supplemental' work (work outside your classification that you may still perform) was amended in 2025.
rules.applies_to: Specialty contractors performing work outside their classification
rules.verbatim_quote: 831 Incidental and Supplemental Defined Amended 2025-26 436
rules.notes: Definition text not in this chunk (Chapter 9). Effective date of the regulatory amendment not stated.

rules.title: Extension of time to correct under an order of correction (16 CCR 883) amended
rules.plain_english: The regulation on getting more time to comply with a CSLB order of correction was amended in 2025.
rules.applies_to: Contractors under a citation order of correction
rules.verbatim_quote: Order of Correction—Extension of 883 Time to Correct Amended 2025-26 516
rules.notes: Extension rules/time periods are NOT in this chunk.

rules.title: Partnership license canceled when a general partner leaves or is added
rules.plain_english: If your license is issued to a general partnership, the license is canceled when any general partner leaves or a new general partner is added.

cancel_triggers: general partner leaves for any reason

rules.citation: B&P (partnership license cancellation; section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: when a contractor’s license is issued to a general partnership and a ... general partner leaves for any reason or the partnership wants to add another general partner, the license is canceled.
rules.notes: Partners may be personally liable for partnership debts and other partners' negligence. Also: a general partnership requires registration of the business name (PDF pages 39-40).

rules.title: LLC: file Articles of Organization (LLC-1); keep operating agreement on site
rules.plain_english: To form an LLC, file Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1) with the Secretary of State; the LLC must also have a members' operating agreement kept at its records office (not filed with the state).

parameters.operating_agreement_kept_at: office where LLC records are kept

rules.citation: California LLC law (section not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition to filing the applicable documents with the Secretary of State, an operating agreement among the members as to the affairs of the LLC and the conduct of its business is required. The LLC does not file the operating agreement with the Secretary of State but maintains it at the office where the LLC’s records are kept.
rules.notes: Form text: 'To form an LLC in California, Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1) must be filed with the California Secretary of State’s office.' LLC licensees also need the $100,000 wage bond and liability insurance (see related rules).

rules.title: Corporations begin by filing articles of incorporation
rules.plain_english: To incorporate, file articles of incorporation with the California Secretary of State.
rules.citation: California Corporations Code (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: You can begin the process of incorporation by filing articles of incorporation with the Secretary of State.
rules.notes: Corporate officers may be personally liable even though stockholders usually are not.

rules.title: Sole owners and partnerships pay estimated taxes quarterly
rules.plain_english: If the business is a sole proprietorship or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.citation: Federal/state tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.notes: Specific quarterly due dates are not stated in this source.

rules.title: Get a federal EIN; deposit withheld payroll taxes on schedule
rules.plain_english: Employers must get a federal Employer Identification Number from the IRS and pay withheld federal income and Social Security taxes quarterly, monthly or semimonthly as required.
rules.citation: Federal tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: A federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) must be requested from the Internal Revenue Service, and the federal income and Social Security taxes withheld from employee wages must be paid quarterly, monthly, or semimonthly, as required.
rules.notes: Which deposit frequency applies is set by IRS rules, not stated here.

rules.title: Register with EDD; pay state payroll taxes for employees earning over $100/quarter
rules.plain_english: Register with California's EDD, get a state employer number, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for any employee who earns more than $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.citation: California Unemployment Insurance Code (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.

rules.title: Seller's permit, possible 6-month sales tax deposit, collect sales tax
rules.plain_english: Businesses selling tangible personal property need a California Seller's Permit, may be required to deposit six months of estimated sales tax, and must collect sales tax from customers unless tax on materials was paid at purchase.

parameters.possible_security_deposit: estimated sales tax for first 6 months
parameters.collect_sales_tax_unless: tax on materials already paid at purchase

rules.applies_to: Contractors that sell tangible personal property (e.g., fixtures/materials sold to customers)
rules.citation: California sales and use tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: California requires a Seller’s Permit for businesses that sell tangible personal property. The State Board of Equalization can require a deposit of the estimated sales tax for the first six months. The contractor must collect the required sales tax from the customer unless the tax on materials is already paid at the time of purchase.
rules.notes: Book names the State Board of Equalization; seller's permit administration has since moved to the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) - verify current agency.

rules.title: Determine city/county permits before starting a job
rules.plain_english: Before starting any job, find out whether city or county permits are required, and know the applicable zoning laws and building codes.
rules.citation: Local ordinances / building codes (not cited on this page)
rules.verbatim_quote: Before starting a job, determine if city or county permits are required. In addition, the contractor must be familiar with zoning laws and building codes.
rules.notes: Ties to the HIC requirement to describe permits and state who pays for them.

rules.title: Project bond cost typically 1-2% of contract price
rules.plain_english: Performance/payment bonds usually cost about 1 to 2 percent of the contract price; include that cost in your bid.
rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding bonded projects (often lender-financed or commercial)
rules.verbatim_quote: Bonds can be obtained from bonding companies for a percentage of the contract price, usually in the one to two percent range. This requirement is the cost of doing business that should be recognized when the bid is submitted.
rules.notes: Industry guidance, not a legal requirement. Bonding is 'generally mandatory for large jobs financed by institutional lenders'.

rules.title: Performance, payment and contract bonds; surety liability capped at face amount
rules.plain_english: Performance bonds guarantee completion, payment bonds protect against labor/material liens, contract bonds do both; the surety generally pays no more than the bond's face amount unless it took over completion.

bond_types.performance_bond: guarantees completion per plans and specs
bond_types.payment_bond: assures owner no liens for labor and materials

parameters.surety_max_liability: face amount of bond (unless surety assumed completion)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on bonded projects
rules.verbatim_quote: In general, unless the bonding company has taken responsibility for completing the project, the bonding company will not have to pay more than the face amount of the bond.
rules.notes: Project bonds are distinct from the contractor license bond.

rules.title: Contractor license bond $25,000; qualifying individual bond $25,000
rules.plain_english: Every licensed contractor must carry a $25,000 contractor license bond; a qualifying individual's bond is also $25,000.

parameters.scope: any project the contractor agrees to perform

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; qualifying individuals where required
rules.citation: B&P contractor bond provisions (section not cited on this page; commonly B&P 7071.6 and 7071.9)
rules.verbatim_quote: Each licensed contractor is required to carry a contractor bond. ... The contractor license bond amount is $25,000. The bond for qualifying individuals is $25,000.
rules.notes: Cash deposit may be filed in lieu of bond (AB 521, PDF page 12). When a qualifying-individual bond is required is not specified in this chunk.

rules.title: LLC licensees need an additional $100,000 employee/worker bond
rules.plain_english: An LLC contractor must carry a $100,000 surety bond for workers, on top of the $25,000 license bond, to issue, reissue, reinstate, reactivate or renew the license.

parameters.beneficiaries: employees/workers damaged by failure to pay wages, interest on wages, fringe benefits, other contributions

rules.applies_to: Contractors licensed as limited liability companies
rules.verbatim_quote: A $100,000 surety bond (in addition to the $25,000 contractor bond) is required for the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, and renewal of an LLC license for the benefit of any employee or worker damaged by the LLC’s failure to pay wages, interest on wages, or fringe benefits, as well as other contributions.
rules.notes: Total bonding for an LLC licensee: $125,000 (25,000 + 100,000).

rules.title: CGL insurance not required by license law except for LLCs
rules.plain_english: California license law doesn't require general liability insurance unless your business is an LLC, though commercial owners commonly require it by contract.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors State License Law does not require contractors to carry CGL insurance unless their business entity is a limited liability company (see below).
rules.notes: Home improvement contractors must still disclose CGL status in writing (16 CCR 872(a)).

rules.title: Home improvement contractors must disclose CGL insurance status in writing
rules.plain_english: Home improvement contractors must tell the homeowner in writing whether they carry general liability insurance, and if so, give the insurer's name and phone number in writing.
rules.verbatim_quote: the California Code of Regulations (CCR) section 872(a), requires home improvement contractors to: ● Disclose in writing if they do or do not carry commercial general liability insurance. ● If they do carry CGL insurance, provide the homeowner with the name and telephone number of the insurance company, in writing, so the homeowner can verify coverage.
rules.notes: Corresponds to the 'Commercial General Liability Insurance' notice in the HIC required-notices list.

rules.title: LLC liability insurance: $1M aggregate + $100K per personnel over 5, max $5M
rules.plain_english: An LLC contractor must carry liability insurance with at least a $1 million aggregate limit if it has five or fewer personnel of record, plus $100,000 for each additional person, up to $5 million.
rules.verbatim_quote: Liability insurance with the aggregate limit of $1 million for licensees with five or fewer people listed as members of the personnel of record is required for a limited liability company; plus, an additional $100,000 in insurance is required for each additional member of the personnel of record, not to exceed $5 million total.
rules.notes: Cap reached at 45 personnel of record (1,000,000 + 40 * 100,000 = 5,000,000).

rules.title: Workers' comp required with one or more employees (even part-time)
rules.plain_english: If you have even one employee, including part-time and employed relatives, you must carry workers' compensation coverage.
rules.citation: Labor Code 3700; see Labor Code 2750.5 (owner-operators/independent contractors)
rules.verbatim_quote: If the employer has one or more employees, even part-time, they are required to insure for workers’ compensation claims.
rules.notes: Employer may be sued for damages if illegally uninsured or if it conceals an employee's injury. 'Owner-operators' and 'independent contractors' should review Labor Code 2750.5. Certain classifications must carry WC even with no employees (see wc-mandatory-classifications).

rules.title: Three ways to secure workers' comp coverage
rules.plain_english: You can cover workers' comp by (1) a standard policy from a licensed carrier, (2) a DIR self-insurance permit, or (3) a collectively bargained alternative dispute resolution program recognized by DWC.

methods: standard approved policy from licensed carrier
self-insurer permit from Director of Department of Industrial Relations (Labor Code 3700)
collectively bargained ADR program recognized by Division of Workers’ Compensation (Labor Code 3201.5)

rules.verbatim_quote: The employer-contractor may provide insurance protection in one of three ways: ● A standard approved policy of workers’ compensation insurance available through any licensed carrier; or ● Securing a permit from the Director of the state Department of Industrial Relations to become a self-insurer (Labor Code §3700); or
rules.notes: Third method (Labor Code 3201.5 collectively bargained ADR program) follows on the same page.

rules.title: Workers' comp penalties the insurer does not absorb
rules.plain_english: Your WC insurer takes on your WC obligations, except penalties for your serious and willful misconduct, injury to an illegally employed worker under 16, or discriminating against an employee for filing a claim.

employer_retains_penalties_for.basis: injury to illegally employed person under 16
discrimination against employee for filing industrial injury claim

rules.verbatim_quote: In general, if a contractor carries workers’ compensation insurance, the workers’ compensation insurance company assumes the obligation of the contractor under the workers’ compensation laws. Some exceptions include penalties based on:
rules.notes: Penalty amounts not stated in this source.

rules.title: Keep a current WC certificate on file with CSLB in the business name
rules.plain_english: Applicants and licensees must always have a current, valid Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance (or self-insurance certification) on file with CSLB in the license's business name; insurers can file it electronically.
rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees with employees (or in WC-mandatory classifications)
rules.verbatim_quote: B&P Code section 7125 provides that an applicant or licensee always has on file a current and valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the licensee’s business name.
rules.notes: Monitor policy expiration dates so the certificate on file never lapses; SB 291 blocks renewal/reinstatement without a valid certificate.

rules.title: File a WC exemption if you have no employees
rules.plain_english: If you have no employees, you must file a workers' comp exemption with CSLB, unless you hold a classification that must carry WC anyway.
rules.verbatim_quote: If you don’t have employees, you must file an exemption from the workers’ compensation requirement unless you hold one of these classifications which requires you to carry workers’ compensation insurance: C-8 Concrete; C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning; C-22 Asbestos Abatement; C-39 Roofing; C-61/D-49 Tree Service.
rules.notes: SB 291 directs CSLB to create an evidence-based verification process for exemptions (PDF page 13).

rules.title: Classifications that must carry WC even with no employees
rules.plain_english: C-8 Concrete, C-20 HVAC, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-39 Roofing and C-61/D-49 Tree Service licensees must carry workers' comp insurance even if they have no employees.
rules.applies_to: Licensees holding any of the listed classifications
rules.verbatim_quote: If you don’t have employees, you must file an exemption from the workers’ compensation requirement unless you hold one of these classifications which requires you to carry workers’ compensation insurance: C-8 Concrete; C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning; C-22 Asbestos Abatement; C-39 Roofing; C-61/D-49 Tree Service.
rules.notes: Check against B&P 7125 full text in Chapter 8 for any additions.

rules.title: Report every lost-time or beyond-first-aid work injury/illness
rules.plain_english: Employers must file a complete report of every employee injury or illness that causes lost time beyond the day of injury or needs more than first aid, with DIR's Division of Labor Statistics and Research, or with the insurer if insured.

reportable_if_any: lost time beyond the date of injury or illness

file_with.uninsured_or_self_insured: DIR Division of Labor Statistics and Research

rules.verbatim_quote: An employer-contractor MUST file a complete report of every employee occupational injury or occupational illness that results in lost time beyond the date of injury or illness, or which requires medical treatment beyond first aid, with the Department of Industrial Relations through its Division of Labor Statistics and Research or, if an insured employer, with the insurer (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: See injury-report-5-day-deadline for timing.

rules.title: File occupational injury/illness report within 5 days of knowledge
rules.plain_english: File the occupational injury or illness report within five days after you learn of the injury or illness.

parameters.trigger: employer obtains knowledge of injury or illness

rules.verbatim_quote: A report shall be filed concerning each injury and illness that has, or is alleged to have, arisen out of and in the course of employment, within ... five days after the employer obtains knowledge of the injury or illness.
rules.notes: Source does not say whether 'days' are calendar or working days.

rules.title: Insured employer must report injuries to insurer; WCAB 5-day order; contempt
rules.plain_english: Insured employers must report every employee injury or illness to their insurer; if they don't, the WCAB can order a report within five days, and ignoring the order can be punished as contempt.
rules.verbatim_quote: If a report is not filed with the insurance carrier, the Workers’ Compensation Appeals Board may issue an order directing the insured employer to report the injury or illness within five ... days. Failure of the employer to comply with this order may be punished as contempt (Labor Code §3760).

rules.title: Report serious injury, illness or death immediately to Cal/OSHA
rules.plain_english: For any serious injury, illness or death, report immediately to the Division of Occupational Safety and Health by phone or email, in addition to the regular injury report.

parameters.agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA)

rules.verbatim_quote: In every case involving a serious injury or illness, or death, in addition to the report described above, the employer must report immediately by telephone or email to the Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: This source does not define an hour limit for 'immediately'; Cal/OSHA regulations do - check them before encoding a numeric deadline.

rules.title: Give new employees written WC rights notice by end of first pay period
rules.plain_english: Give every new employee written notice of their workers' comp rights at hire or by the end of their first pay period, using DWC-approved content, in English and Spanish if you have Spanish-speaking employees.

parameters.deadline: at time of hire or by end of first pay period
parameters.content_spec: approved by DWC Administrative Director; info in 8 CCR 9880

rules.verbatim_quote: Give every new employee, either at the time of hiring or by the end of their first pay period, written notice of the employee’s right to receive workers’ compensation benefits should they be injured on the job while working for the employer.
rules.notes: Onboarding checklist item; due date computable from hire date + first pay period end.

rules.title: Post WC Notice to Employees poster (misdemeanor if not posted)
rules.plain_english: Conspicuously post the workers' comp 'Notice to Employees' poster where employees frequent, in English and Spanish if you have Spanish-speaking employees; failing to keep it posted is a misdemeanor.

parameters.content_spec: 8 CCR 9881 or approved poster in 8 CCR 9881.1

rules.verbatim_quote: Post conspicuously, in a location frequented by employees, a Notice to Employees poster. ... Failure to keep such a notice conspicuously posted is punishable as a misdemeanor (Labor Code §3550).

rules.title: Post occupational safety and health rights and citations
